prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CC(C)CN(C[C@@H](O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)O[C@H]1CO[C@H]2OCC[C@H]21)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(N)cc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL243

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of HIV1 protease by FRET assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant HIV1 protease measured assessed as hydrolysis of fluorogenic substrate by FRET assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call":"COMMENSURABLE","confidence":0.93,"error_class":"none","reason":"Both assays measure inhibition of the same HIV-1 protease target using a fluorogenic-substrate FRET format, with no indicated differences in construct, organism, or readout."}

parsed.reason: Both assays measure inhibition of the same HIV-1 protease target using a fluorogenic-substrate FRET format, with no indicated differences in construct, organism, or readout.
